pr.title: We don't need `NonNull::as_ptr` debuginfo
pr.description:
In order to stop pessimizing the use of local variables in core, skip debug info for MIR temporaries in tiny (single-BB) functions.

For functions as simple as this -- `Pin::new`, etc -- nobody every actually wants debuginfo for them in the first place.  They're more like intrinsics than real functions, and stepping over them is good.
pr.author: scottmcm

processing.reason: The historical change in PR #133899 is the new StripDebugInfo MIR pass, which only filters `body.var_debug_info` (debug metadata). It does not rewrite any MIR assignment, local value, control flow, or return value: the only code is a `retain` over `VarDebugInfoContents`, keeping Place entries for argument locals (and excluding RETURN_PLACE) when `-Zmir_strip_debuginfo` is not `None`. The PR itself introduces no miscompile claim, and the frozen analysis explicitly warns not to invent a different wrong rewrite. Therefore there is no source-grounded original/transformed pair whose defined executions produce different runtime values under Miri. Any pair demonstrating a numeric/boolean/character difference would be an unrelated fabricated program, not the historical transformation. The correct regression test for this PR is a MIR-dump/metadata test (already added as tests/mir-opt/strip_debuginfo.rs), not a runtime counterexample.

analysis.summary: The PR adds a StripDebugInfo MIR pass that conditionally deletes non-parameter VarDebugInfo so debug info for MIR temporaries in tiny single-basic-block functions (e.g. core's Pin::new/NonNull::as_ptr wrappers) no longer pessimizes later optimization. It is an optimization/enabling cleanup, not a confirmed semantic bug fix. The pass runs after the final SimplifyCfg because its tiny-function mode requires one-block functions.
analysis.originalLogic: Before this PR, every MIR VarDebugInfo entry was retained for all functions, including debug entries for compiler-generated temporaries and nested inlined scopes. The PR describes the motivation as: "In order to stop pessimizing the use of local variables in core, skip debug info for MIR temporaries in tiny (single-BB) functions." There was no pass that conditionally removed these entries.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historically pessimistic behavior was to keep all VarDebugInfo entries unchanged (do not strip) even for tiny primitive-like wrappers. The corrected transformation is conditional removal: in LocalsInTinyFunctions mode, only bodies whose START_BLOCK terminator is Return are stripped; in AllLocals mode all bodies are stripped. In both stripping modes the retain predicate preserves only VarDebugInfoContents::Place entries whose place.local.as_usize() <= body.arg_count and place.local != RETURN_PLACE. No runtime MIR assignment or semantic value is changed by this pass; only debug metadata is removed. Do not invent a different wrong rewrite: this PR does not claim a miscompile was fixed.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR bodies with var_debug_info entries compiled with -Zmir_strip_debuginfo set to one of None, LocalsInTinyFunctions, or AllLocals. Relevant distinctions: single-basic-block body ending in Return versus multi-block body (e.g. a loop); debug entries that are Place-based parameter locals versus non-parameter/temporary locals; Place debug entries versus Const debug entries such as PhantomData constants; functions that are later inlined versus functions remaining as callers.
analysis.trigger: StripDebugInfo is enabled when sess.opts.unstable_opts.mir_strip_debuginfo != MirStripDebugInfo::None. For the tiny-function mode, it activates only when the first block's terminator is TerminatorKind::Return. In the MIR pipeline it is scheduled immediately after simplify::SimplifyCfg::Final with the source comment "After the last SimplifyCfg, because this wants one-block functions."
preconditions: The pass must run after the final SimplifyCfg so that functions intended to be recognized as tiny are already single-block when stripping is considered.
For LocalsInTinyFunctions, the START_BLOCK terminator must be TerminatorKind::Return; merely having one block is not sufficient if the terminator is something else.
The body must have var_debug_info entries; the pass retains entries only when value is VarDebugInfoContents::Place and the local is an argument (local <= arg_count) and is not RETURN_PLACE.
The -Zmir_strip_debuginfo option must not be None; bootstrap passes locals-in-tiny-functions for non-stage0 compiler builds.
pitfalls: Do not confuse debuginfo stripping with changing MIR dataflow or runtime behavior: local assignments and values remain; only var_debug_info is filtered. The vec_deref test local renumbering reflects later optimization after debug entries no longer constrain/influence the pipeline, not a direct value rewrite by StripDebugInfo.

Do not preserve every parameter blindly: the filter matches only Place-based entries. Const-valued debug entries are removed even when they describe an argument-like component, as seen with the removed PhantomData constant debug line.
Do not apply the tiny-function condition by counting blocks alone without checking that the terminator is Return; the implementation checks body.basic_blocks[START_BLOCK].terminator().kind.
Do not move StripDebugInfo before the last SimplifyCfg: functions that become single-BB only after simplification would not be recognized as tiny.

When interpreting inline tests, remember callee debug info may have been stripped before inlining; removal of a nested 'debug pointer => _3;' from an inlined Pin::new_unchecked scope does not mean StripDebugInfo rewrote the caller body directly.
Do not assume AllLocals is restricted to tiny functions: it is the mode that strips everywhere, while LocalsInTinyFunctions preserves debug info in looping/multi-block functions.
analysis.testStrategy: Use a mir-opt test with revisions NONE, TINY, and ALL selected by -Zmir_strip_debuginfo=none, -Zmir_strip_debuginfo=locals-in-tiny-functions, and -Zmir_strip_debuginfo=all-locals. Include (1) a tiny single-block function with a parameter and two let-bound temporaries, and (2) a looping multi-block function with a parameter and loop locals. Check that the parameter debug entry is present in all revisions, that tiny-function locals appear only under NONE, that looping-function locals appear under NONE and TINY but not ALL, and that ALL removes non-parameter locals everywhere. Also inspect inlined MIR dumps to verify nested debug entries from tiny callees disappear, and keep codegen CHECK lines flexible about local numbering. No execution/reproduction is needed or claimed.
evidence: In order to stop pessimizing the use of local variables in core, skip debug info for MIR temporaries in tiny (single-BB) functions.
After the last SimplifyCfg, because this wants one-block functions.
